newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dlr ends little changed pre-RBNZ, trade whippy.
newsitem.headline: NZ dlr ends little changed pre-RBNZ, trade whippy.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed little changed after Treasury's pre-election opening of the government's books but dealers said trade was whippy and nervous before Friday's Reserve Bank economic projections.
The currency remained well supported in good two-way business, closing at US$0.6960/67 and a shade above 66.0 on its Trade-Weighted Index.
A Wellington dealer said Treasury's Economic and Fiscal Update was in line with expectations, predicting a gradual easing in monetary conditions from the December quarter.

A second dealer said the forecasts, particularly on growth and government surpluses, should be taken with a pinch of salt, especially in the light of a hard-to-call general election on October 12 which economists expect to herald looser fiscal policy.

Treasury still sees growth of 2.5 percent in the year to March 1997, little changed from the 2.6 percent it forecast in the May budget, whereas most private sector economists see growth below two percent.
Budget surpluses were forecast by Treasury to rise to more than $6 billion by 2000.
While economists unanimously forecast no easing from the Reserve Bank, a dealer said he thought the bank may favour a somewhat lower currency.

"The Reserve Bank, for me, want the interest rate yields higher and the currency lower...Of course they've got to be careful that they don't signal a weaker exchange rate and then have an election result that sees it come off badly even further. So they will have some trepidation about saying that the currency can go weaker, but if anything that's what they will allude to," he said.
